 Duke vs. Michigan State game preview
 Duke's first two games offered almost zero suspense. Jon Scheyer's Blue Devils followed an 84-50 victory over Army with a 113-52 dismantling of Coastal Carolina. Patrick Ngongba II scored a career-high 28 in the second game and grabbed nine rebounds, shooting 10-for-13 from the field. Cayden Boozer contributed 11 points and 12 assists with just one turnover. John Blackwell and Caleb Foster scored 15 apiece, while Dame Sarr added 12. Duke assisted on 26 of its 38 made field goals and outrebounded Coastal Carolina 53-27. 
 Those numbers explain the fast start, but Michigan State should present a far tougher test in the paint. The Blue Devils have scored at least 50 points inside in both games.
 Michigan State has handled its opening assignments just as decisively, beating Quinnipiac 96-59 and Toledo 91-61. Tom Izzo's offense runs through Jeremy Fears Jr., who's averaging 12.5 points and 10 assists. Fears opened with 13 points and 11 assists against Quinnipiac. Jordan Scott has provided 11.5 points and 7.5 rebounds per game, while Anton Bonke collected 13 rebounds in the opener. The Spartans reached the Sweet Sixteen last season, but they're replacing two starting frontcourt players. That's a relevant concern against Duke's interior depth. 
 There's history here, too. Duke leads the all-time series 16-4 and has taken the last three meetings, including a 66-60 game last December. Fears dished out 13 assists in that defeat, so he's already seen how Duke defends this matchup. Michigan State has a chance to respond in the Champions Classic, where it defeated Kentucky last season.  Sign up now to make college basketball trades and get a $25 bonus with the Polymarket promo code CBSSPORTS: 
 Duke vs. Michigan State prediction
 The first challenge for Michigan State is protecting the ball without taking the pace out of its own offense. Fears has delivered 20 assists against seven turnovers through two games, and the Spartans will need that passing to work against a much more disruptive defense. Duke recorded 16 steals against Army and 12 more against Coastal Carolina. The Blue Devils also held Coastal Carolina to 30.2% shooting and opened the game with 16 unanswered points. 
 A few hurried possessions could put the Spartans behind before their offense finds a rhythm. Izzo can ask Fears to work through the half court, but Duke has enough length to challenge passes into the lane. Michigan State can't count on the same open looks it found in its first two outings.
 Duke has more than one way to create those problems. Boozer's 12-assist performance against Coastal Carolina showed how effectively he can move the ball without hunting his own shot. Ngongba supplies scoring near the rim, and freshman Joaquim Boumtje Boumtje has already blocked six shots in two games. Michigan State has capable rebounders, but replacing last season's starting post players adds another challenge against Duke's size. 
 The SportsLine model puts Duke ahead 80-69, an 11-point victory. It also gives the Blue Devils a 64% simulation rate to win by at least eight points.
